title: He didn’t obey her like a servant.
paragraphs: He didn’t obey her like a servant.
But He didn’t ignore her either.
That tension… that’s where the truth lives.
In John 2, at the wedding in Cana, Mary says one simple line:
No command. No demand. Just a need.
“Woman, what does this have to do with me? My hour has not yet come.” (John 2:4)

That sounds sharp to modern ears—but in that culture, “Woman” was respectful, not rude. Still, don’t miss it:
Jesus is drawing a boundary.
He’s saying: “I am no longer acting under human timing—even yours. I move according to My Father.”
Because Jesus is not just her son.

Mary doesn’t argue.
She doesn’t pull rank as “mother.”
She doesn’t force control.
She turns to the servants and says:
That line… that’s her real authority.

Not control over Jesus.
But complete trust in Him.

Mary had a unique role—chosen, honored, blessed among women (Luke 1:28).
But she was still a sinner in need of a Savior (Luke 1:47).
She didn’t command the Son of God.
Jesus performs the miracle—not because He was ordered…
So does Mary have authority over Jesus?

Even as a child, He submitted to her (Luke 2:51).
But as the Messiah, He submits only to the will of the Father (John 6:38).
And maybe that’s the real question for us:
Are you trying to control Jesus…
Because many of us treat God like He’s under our instruction:

“Lord, fix this.”
“Lord, do it now.”
“Lord, follow my plan.”
But heaven doesn’t move on our command.
It moves on His perfect will.
The same Jesus who said “My hour has not yet come”…
Someone you love is trying to control what only Jesus can redeem.
